# Direct-speech fixtures

Labelled short clips for the voice service's direct-speech gate: the acoustic
decision that keeps a VAD turn away from STT, and the content judgement that
runs on the transcript afterwards. Five classes, one directory each:

| Directory | Verdict | What the clip is |
|---|---|---|
| `holder-direct/` | A | the holder speaking close to the device |
| `other-direct/` | A' | a different person speaking close to the device |
| `side-talk/` | B | two people talking to each other near the device |
| `background-tv/` | C | TV or radio speech heard at a distance |
| `background-noise/` | C | household noise, no speech |

46 clips, 153.4 s, 4.68 MiB — 10 `holder-direct` (6 en, 4 es), 10 `other-direct`
(5 en, 5 es), 8 `side-talk` (4 en, 4 es, each a two-speaker exchange), 10
`background-tv` (5 en, 5 es), 8 `background-noise` (generated).

## Format

Raw mono PCM, signed 16-bit little-endian, 16 kHz, no header — `.bin`, the same
shape as the identity voiceprint fixtures, so the repository's own gates treat
the files as data and a C++ suite reads them with no decoder. The clip path is
`<class>/<id>.bin`; `seconds` in the manifest is the file size divided by
32 000.

`manifest.json` is `{version, ffmpeg, sampleRate, channels, clips}` — the tool
version and the raw-PCM shape at the top, one entry per clip below:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | clip id, unique across the corpus, the file stem |
| `class` | `holder-direct`, `other-direct`, `side-talk`, `background-tv`, `background-noise` |
| `lang` | `es`, `en`, or `none` for the synthetic noise clips |
| `seconds` | exact length of the committed file |
| `source` | dataset or `synthetic` |
| `url` | retrieval URL of the dataset, empty for synthetic clips |
| `license` | `CC0-1.0`, `CC-BY-4.0` or `synthetic` |
| `speaker` | dataset speaker id (`5694`, `cv-es:0f0a130d83e6`, `5694+3000` for an exchange), empty for synthetic clips |
| `processing` | the exact chain applied, its level target and the level the committed file actually measures |
| `sha256` | sha256 of the committed file |

Every clip is level-normalised — a target RMS with a peak ceiling, so nothing
clips — because level relative to the holder's running level is one of the cues
the gate reads. The direct classes sit at −20 dBFS RMS (the second voice of a
side-talk clip at −21.5), `background-tv` carries its source speech at −14,
−16, −18 and −20 dB below that with a low-pass, a short reverb, a generated
music bed and a pink floor, and `background-noise` sweeps −14 to −42 dBFS RMS.
A level threshold can therefore be swept over the corpus instead of checked at
a single point. The peak ceiling binds on six direct clips (peak exactly
−1.00 dBFS, so their RMS lands between −20.32 and −23.65), which is why every
row records the measured level beside the target rather than only the target.
`--only` refuses to write into this directory: a partial manifest would
silently shrink the ground truth the runner reads.

The `background-noise` clips and the beds mixed into `background-tv` are
generated by the build script. Every other clip is public speech: the direct
ones trimmed, the `side-talk` ones a concatenation of two speakers' utterances
with the turn gaps written in.

## Provenance

Common Voice 17.0 Spanish test split (CC0-1.0) and Mini LibriSpeech
`dev-clean-2` (CC-BY-4.0), plus ffmpeg-generated noise. No private recording is
part of the corpus, and no NC- or ND-licensed material is used. Per-source
licences, attribution and retrieval URLs are in `licenses/sources.md`.

## Rebuild

```bash
python3 -I services/voice/scripts/direct-speech-fixtures.py
```

The script downloads its sources into `models/voice-fixtures-cache/`
(gitignored) and rewrites the clips, `manifest.json` and nothing else; only
processed clips, the manifest and the licence notes are committed. Adding
clips means adding rows to the `CLIPS` table in the script.

## Measure

Once the gate exists, a harness classifies every clip and writes one JSON line
per clip (`{"id": ..., "predicted": ...}`), and

```bash
python3 -I services/voice/tests/eval/direct-speech-eval.py --classifications <file.jsonl>
```

prints the per-class precision/recall, the confusion matrix, the direct-speech
false-reject rate (target ≤ 1 %), the side-talk false-positive rate and the
background false-positive rate. Without `--classifications` it exits 77; a
classifications file that does not cover every manifest id exits 2; the
direct-speech false-reject target missed exits 1.
